comparator.route: Social Networks year-two field and project; Labour Sociology year-three field course
comparator.sourceNotes: The current programme-specific regulations account for the full 180 EC: 60 EC compulsory in year one; 45 EC fixed sociology and methods, one 5-EC field course and its corresponding 10-EC project in year two; and a 30-EC broadening minor, 25 EC fixed work and one different 5-EC field course in year three. The normalized registry target names the general bachelor and supplies no student-specific field preference. The route therefore uses the first listed year-two field course (Social Networks), its required corresponding project, and then the first listed year-three field course not already taken (Labour Sociology), before considering UCR fit. The 30-EC broadening minor remains genuine approved choice space. The official current bachelor page independently confirms the 180-EC duration, field-specialisation structure and live curriculum.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target does not name one of the four field specialisations. The formal 2026–2027 regulations list Social Networks first for the year-two choose-one set and require the project to correspond, so Social Networks and Project Social Networks are selected. Year three requires one field course not already taken; Labour Sociology is the first remaining item in the same official list. This neutral source-order decision was made before assessing UCR fit.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Sociological theory about institutions, relationships, norms, inequality and social change
Qualitative and quantitative social research, statistics, data collection and evidence-based analysis
Social welfare, education, work, health and unequal life chances
Applied projects, policy research, professional development and an independent sociology thesis
adjacent: Work, organisations, markets, public institutions and organisational inequality
Crime, public safety, cybercrime, law and institutional responses
Social networks, media, collective behaviour, health and ageing
questions: How do social institutions and relationships create or reduce public problems and inequality?
How can mixed social evidence be translated into policy and practical solutions?
How do digital media, neighbourhoods and collective behaviour shape social values and safety?

alternatives.label: Sociology, inequality & social research
alternatives.concept: Study social theory, inequality and collective action. Use interviews, statistics and data analysis to investigate institutions, public health, media and policy.
alternatives.labelReason: Five dedicated Sociology courses and a substantial qualitative, statistical and data-analysis spine anchor the schedule; its supporting courses consistently address inequality, institutions, public problems and social change.
progression: Economics starts in the first term and Comparative Politics moves to the third. Introductory sociology and research methods precede the more advanced work. The programme has 7 advanced courses and passes current offering and prerequisite checks.

alternatives.label: Work, organisations & social inequality
alternatives.concept: Study how workplaces, markets and public policy affect opportunity and inequality. Combine sociology with organisational psychology, negotiation, public economics and econometrics.
alternatives.labelReason: Organisational psychology, negotiation, public economics and econometrics support a sociology-led programme about work and inequality.
alternatives.distinctness: 8 courses and 60 EC differ from the broad option in each direction. This option gives more weight to workplaces, bargaining and economic policy.
progression: Economics begins in the first term. Data Science moves to the fourth term and Rhetoric in Action moves to the sixth. Research methods precede Public Economics, advanced leadership and econometrics. The programme has 6 advanced courses and passes current offering and prerequisite checks.

alternatives.label: Crime, public safety & social institutions
alternatives.concept: Study how social institutions respond to crime and threats to public safety. Combine sociology with criminal justice, social movements, conflict, youth resilience and research methods.
alternatives.labelReason: Criminal justice, conflict and youth resilience support a sociology-led study of public safety and institutional responses.
alternatives.distinctness: This option differs from the first by 8 courses and from the second by 10 courses in each direction. Criminal justice, youth resilience and evidence synthesis give it a distinct emphasis.
progression: Human Rights moves to the third term and Criminal Law follows the law gateway in the fifth. Social Movements & Environmental Justice adds a direct sociology component before advanced evidence synthesis. The programme has 7 advanced courses and passes current offering and prerequisite checks.

selection.assessment: Three sociology-led options are supported. They focus on broad social inquiry, work and organisations, and public safety. Each pair differs by at least 8 courses in each direction. The public safety option centres on institutions and social risks without promising specialist digital-crime study.

blocks: Sociological theory, social order and change
Both introduce sociological concepts and explanations. UCR applies them to topics including inequality, social boundaries and institutions.
Both study social change. UCR concentrates on collective action and environmental justice, while Groningen gives wider attention to institutions.
Both use advanced social theories to interpret society. UCR emphasises civil society, trust and critical theory.

Both design empirical studies and collect data. UCR combines this with introductory inference and a group research project.
Both develop qualitative research design and interpretation. UCR includes interviews, focus groups, ethnography and ethical reflection.
Both analyse group comparisons and categorical outcomes through statistical models. UCR focuses on behavioural data and experimental design.

notes.text: Groningen builds a sociology sequence with four statistics courses, two qualitative-methods courses, field projects and a compulsory thesis. UCR covers related theory and methods across disciplines. Its optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a broadening minor. Students choose university minors or seek approval for a personal minor outside Sociology.

audience.programmeDescription: Sociology at the University of Groningen examines how people, groups and institutions shape society. Students study theory and research methods, carry out field projects and complete a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options combine sociology and social research in three options focused on inequality and public issues, work and organisations, or crime and public safety.
